html:
The Seri, who call themselves Comca'ac, are a people of the desert coast of Sonora in north-west Mexico, facing the Gulf of California, and of Tiburón Island. Their language is an isolate, related to no other living language.

They lived as hunters, gatherers and fishers, travelling in reed boats, hunting sea turtles and gathering mesquite pods and cactus fruit, and they never took up farming. Jesuit and later Mexican efforts to settle them in missions largely failed, and they fought Spanish and Mexican forces into the late 1800s, while their neighbours the Tohono O'odham and Yaqui were drawn into colonial life. War and disease brought them close to extinction in the early 1900s. Today about a thousand Seri live in Punta Chueca and El Desemboque, and Tiburón Island is their communal land. They are known for ironwood carving and baskets. Across the gulf lived the Guaycura.
